tts: As figures show that more and more children are overweight, the government has announced that highly competitive sports days and tournaments are to be re-introduced at schools.
Under the new plans, schools will play against each other in an Olympics-style event, with sports such as football, athletics, rugby, swimming, tennis and cycling.
Winning teams will compete in sixty county competitions before going on to a national final.
For too long, schools have been avoiding competitive sports, introducing activities such as yoga, trampolining, cheerleading and dancing instead.
We have to realize that taking part in competitive sport is not bad for people’s self-esteem. Whether you win or lose, competitive sport teaches people to work together in a team.
It is also hoped that the new plans will help the country to break more records in future Olympic Games.

items.q: Why has the government made the announcement?
o: Because figures show more children are overweight
Because the Olympics are being held there

items.q: What have schools been doing instead of competitive sport?
What does the announcement claim about competitive sport?
o: It teaches people to work in a team

tts: It’s just unrealistic for children to be told that everyone can win. Life is competitive. If you lose a race, then you should just try harder.
I don’t think more competition is the answer. Sport at school isn’t about teaching children how to be competitive; it’s about encouraging them to exercise.
There are plenty of children who don’t do well academically, who are brilliant at sport. Why shouldn’t they be allowed to play against each other?
I went to a school that insisted on competitive sports. The school used to hold sports days in a public park, so everyone could watch. I was small for my age and always came last. It was awful.
Competition is healthy, but taking part is more important than winning.
If everyone knows at the start of a race who the winner is going to be, then it can be boring and demotivating.

write.q: Write your view on competitive sport for children. Use at least one general statement with no article, one a/an for a first mention, one the for the second mention of the same thing, and one superlative with the.
plan: one school or team you knew (first mention → second mention)
write.model: In general, I think competitive sport does children more good than harm, although I understand why people disagree. I went to a school where every sports day was held in the public park. The school did it deliberately, so that parents could watch, and for a small child who always came last it was the worst two hours of the year. The strongest argument against competition is exactly that: if everybody already knows who the winner will be, the race is demotivating for everyone else. But I would not remove it. I would change what is measured. The most useful thing anybody taught me at school was how to be a good loser, and you cannot learn that in a class where nobody loses.

speak.q: Talk for about a minute: should schools run competitive sports days? Give your general view, one example from your own school, and the best argument on the other side.
speak.model: In general I think competition does children more good than harm. I went to a school where sports day was held in the public park so parents could watch — and for a small child who always came last, it was the worst two hours of the year. The best argument against it is that if everyone knows who’ll win, the race is demotivating. But I’d keep it. Learning to be a good loser is the most useful thing anybody taught me at school.
